Commentary.Commentary: That's all we have from this absorbing Test match. Important points gained by England for the ICC World Test Championship. The second Test match starts on Friday, 10th June 2022 at 3.30 pm IST (10 am GMT) but as usual, our build-up will begin in advance. Until then, it's goodbye and cheers!

Joe Root is the Player of the Match! The former England skipper talks about his hundred and says that it's fantastic and more importantly, they won the game after such a long time. Adds that it's been a tough road for everyone and he has enjoyed this game and looking forward to the rest of the summer. Hopes that they can use this as a way to step forward. Shares that they always get fantastic support at this ground and it's nice to see them get their money back as well. On playing under Ben Stokes, Root replies that the transition has been smooth and mentions that Ben Stokes won England a number of Test matches under his leadership, and it's a great chance for Root to give back to him. Tells that he loves batting and wants to score as many runs as he can and again make England the best Test team.

Ben Stokes, the victorious captain of England, calls it an amazing Test match to be a part of. Tells that regardless of being captain, the first Test of the English summer is always special due to all the buzz and the build-up. Further says that it was a special week and this win makes it even better. On his rapport with Brendon McCullum, Stokes replies that it's going pretty good with him and he has enjoyed the first week working with him. Adds that there is a change of mindset for everyone, this is a great start and he is happy that everybody operated well this week. Stokes mentions that no one had the upper hand at any stage as this game ebbed and flowed. Regarding Root's hundred and 10,000 runs, Stokes calls him Mr Dependable. On the debut of Matthew Potts, Stokes replies that he loved it and he has been tracking his progress in a Durham shirt. Talks about the impact Potts created every time he got the ball and praises him for his amazing attitude. Praises the knocks of Alex Lees and Jonny Bairstow, and is happy with the attitude shown by them. Smiles and adds that seeing Broad and Anderson still running in and delivering for England inspires them.

Kane Williamson, the captain of New Zealand, starts by saying that the game ebbed and flowed the whole time. Tells that it was tough against the new ball but then it changed. Mentions that they came this morning with high hopes and thought there might be some assistance from the overhead conditions but it wasn't to be. Feels that it's about moving on quickly and taking the learnings. Regarding him trying his best to get the ball changed, Williamson replies that it was pretty difficult and he thought if they get it changed, they might get something going. Calls it a fantastic game and it took an incredible knock from Joe Root to take England home. On Root completing 10,000 Test runs, Kane terms it an unbelievable achievement. States that everybody wants to be contributing more and there was a lot of assistance with the harder ball, so the top order will have to work hard. He is looking forward to the next challenge.
Presentation time...

As mentioned earlier, this Test match wasn't a straightforward one. Momentum was no one's friend, and it kept changing sides quicker than the tennis ball does at Roland Garros. England bounced back. Stuart Broad was at the centre of this comeback. His two wickets and then a run out in the same over through Ollie Pope's direct hit stole New Zealand's advantage. At one stage what looked like a lead above 350, remained 276, and the hosts earned themselves a chance to go 1-0 up in the series.

The second day also started with six wickets in the morning session, and we thought, this Test won't see the next day. But as the saying goes, cricket is a game of great uncertainties. Daryl Mitchell and Tom Blundell joined forces to rescue the touring team. Their 195-run stand took the wind out of England's sails, and by the end of Day 2, New Zealand got into the position to dictate terms. Did they do that?

Let's quickly run through the ebbs and flows of the first Test of this English summer. It was expected to be a batting beauty at Lord's, and both skippers had the same thought in mind - to bat first. Kane Williamson had his say, but things didn't go as planned. Although there weren't any demons on the surface, there was just enough juice to extract. The trio of Anderson, Broad and Potts combined to make full use of the conditions and blew away the Kiwis inside two sessions. New Zealand though didn't sit back regretting and retorted by picking seven English wickets by Stumps on Day 1.

England have done it! They've won this roller-coaster of a Test match. With 61 needed this morning, and five wickets in the tank, the hosts made sure there were no hiccups. The start to the chase was a bit iffy for the hosts, but once Ben Stokes got a life (bowled off a no ball on 1), he and Root constructed a 90-run stand to make things smooth. The former skipper then allied with Ben Foakes to raise an unbeaten match-winning century stand to take England home. Root also went on to complete his maiden century in the fourth innings of a Test match and notched up 10,000 Test runs - only the second Englishman to achieve this feat after Sir Alastair Cook.

Joe Root leads everyone off the park! A great knock. It's a huge ovation for him. No drama in the morning. England stayed focused. New Zealand didn't get the movement they needed and looked lacklustre. Kane Williamson tried hard to convince the umpires to change the ball but in vain. Interestingly, they had one ball changed before as well, and after that, the degree of movement they got was a lot lesser than the previous time. These little things matter sometimes.

FOUR! Here is the winning shot! Joe Root has done it. New era, new England, a new captain and they start with a thumping win over New Zealand. Back of a length, around off, Root goes back and smacks it over mid-wicket for a boundary. Root jumps in delight and the English balcony is on its feet. ENGLAND WIN BY 5 WICKETS!
Width there, short and outside off, Root strokes it through the line but the point fielder makes a diving stop.
Almost drags it on! Southee gets a length ball to bend back in down the slope, Root sticks back to cut but it takes the bottom edge and goes on the bounce to the keeper.
FOUR! Root is in a hurry, two more needed! This one is full and outside off, Root presses forward and creams his drive through mid off.
FOUR! Finds the gap at last! A touch short in length and outside off, Root stays on the back foot and delicately guides it through the gap between gully and wide slip for a boundary.

Drinks break. The ball has not moved much and New Zealand have been unable to pick a single wicket this morning. England have batted positively, mainly Ben Foakes, and they are now 10 runs away from sealing the deal.
A low full toss outside off, Root reaches out and strokes it to deep cover for a single.
Fuller and on middle, it's driven back towards the bowler.
Gets behind the line of the delivery and blocks it to covers.
Pitches it up and around middle, Root drives it down to mid off.
Back of a length, on off and angling away, Foakes gets across the stumps and glances it to deep square leg for another run.
Boult returns to bowl again. Delivers it on a length around leg, it's worked behind square leg for a single.
Movement in the air and off the pitch too as it lands on a fuller length, around middle, Root inside-edges his attempted flick shot down to fine leg. A single taken.
Full and around off, angling in, Joe gets forward and pushes it to mid on.
Fuller and on off, defended back.

HUNDRED FOR ROOT! What a knock under pressure from the former England skipper! This will be one of those satisfying knocks as a batter! Always special when it comes while batting last in a Test match and in a winning cause. 26th Test hundred for Joe and he also completes 10000 Test runs. The Lord's goes Roooooooooooo... What a player!!! Fuller in length and around middle, Root clips it to deep mid-wicket and scampers back for the second run. Off goes the helmet and here comes the applause. This is his first Test ton in the fourth innings. 14 needed more.
Serves it around off, angling in, Root forces it from the back foot to covers.
Serves it on a good length and outside off, Root stays on the back foot and taps it down to gully.
Short and on off, Foakes pulls it through square leg for a couple. 16 needed more.
Delivers it outside off, Foakes plays it down from the back foot to gully.
Around off, on a length, Foakes gets back to work it on the leg side but it takes a soft leading edge and rolls to covers.
Serves it on a length and outside off, Ben commits himself forward and defends it carefully towards gully.
On a length and outside off, going straight on, Foakes has nothing to do.
Lands it on a length and outside off, Root gets across and tucks it through mid-wicket for one. The century stand comes up!
Full and on middle, flicked behind square leg for a run. 19 more for a win, Root three away from a century and New Zealand are 5 overs away from the new ball.

EDGY FOUR! Luck is with England. Root moves to 96. Short and outside off, Root rocks back to cut but it nips back down the hill, takes the inside edge, beats the stumps and keeper. It scoots down to fine leg for a boundary.
Angling in from around off, a length ball, Foakes tucks it through backward square leg and takes one.
Uses the angle of the bowler and works a length ball to mid-wicket.

FOUR! Pulled and pulled well! Short in length and around middle, Ben Foakes immediately goes on the back foot to ride the bounce and pulls it with authority through square leg for a boundary. Foakes has looked very positive this morning, taking the pressure off Root.
Fuller in length and outside off, Foakes is on the front foot and defends it solidly. 29 more to win.
Root is eyeing that gap between slips and gully but so far has failed to pierce it. On a length and outside off, Joe runs it down late but once again the gully fielder makes the stop.
Delivers it on a length and outside off, from wide of the crease, Root gets behind and defends it to mid on.
Beaten this time! A bit short again, outside off and staying down, Root once more attempts to lean back and cut but gets beaten.
Picks out gully. Short in length and around off, Root leans back and tries to guide it down to third man but the gully fielder intervenes with a dive to make the stop.
FOUR! Fantastic straight drive, this time from the blade of Root. Fullish and around off, Joe strides forward and strokes it elegantly down the ground for a boundary. Moves into the 90s.
A touch short and around off, Root plays nice and late, from the back foot but it goes straight to the fielder at gully.
Again Kane Williamson reports an issue with the ball. This is the second or the third time this morning. The umpire checks it but finds it fine to continue.
Pitches it up and around off, Foakes drives but finds the mid off fielder.
A little bit of movement on this delivery. Full and around off, Foakes tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Around off, on a length, Foakes defends it solidly from the back foot.
Shortish and outside off, Ben cuts from the crease but finds point.
This one keeps a bit low from a length around off, Foakes stays focused and defends it out safely on the leg side.
Bowls it full but on the pads, Root whips it behind square leg and rotates the strike.
Slightly short in length and outside off, Foakes shoulders arms. 34 needed more.
Finds the gap! It's on a length and outside off, Foakes leans forward, doesn't try to it hard, just pushes it with great timing through covers. Two more.
Bouncer around off, Ben Foakes picks it nice and early before ducking.
Back of a length, around off, Ben goes on the back foot and taps it down to point. New Zealand are going through the motions with nothing happening off the pitch.
FOUR! Pristine timing! Full in length and around off, Foakes shows the full face of his bat and  caresses it past the mid on fielder for a boundary.
Angles in a length ball on off, Foakes works it off his pads but fails to beat the diving short mid-wicket fielder.
Fine shot for nothing! Fuller in length and outside off, Root plays an eye-catching cover drive but fails to find the gap. 40 more to win. England have added 21 runs in the 6 overs this morning.
Back of a length, around leg and middle, Ben glances it through square leg and picks up a single.
A near-yorker on off, Foakes brings his bat down in time and digs it out back towards the bowler.
Bouncer to Foakes, around middle and leg, he ducks easily.
Short in length, around leg, Root turns inside the crease and pulls it down to fine leg for one.
On a length and around middle, Root gets back and plays late but still finds gully.

Vital stop with no third man in place. Around off, on a length, Ben plays late at it and guides it towards third man. Tom Latham immediately moves across to his right from second slip, dives and saves a certain boundary.
FOUR! Excellent shot. The length goes slightly short and outside off, Foakes eases himself on the back foot and packs a punch through point for a glorious boundary. 42 needed more.
Fullish and around off, Foakes drives it down the ground but finds mid off.
Hurls a length ball in the channel outside off, Foakes covers his stumps and shoulders arms.
Outside off, left alone.
Shortish and on off, Root moves back and drops it with gentle hands to mid-wicket. Calls for a run and gets it comfortably.
Lands it on a length around leg, angling across, Foakes stays on the back foot and jams it down safely. 47 needed more.
Close to off, on a length and angling away again, Foakes lunges and defends it with an angled bat to the off side.
Angling away from the batter, outside off and on a length, Ben Foakes doesn't flirt with it.
Trent Boult switches to over the wicket...
Digs it in short, outside off, Fokaes stays back and plays it down to point. He lets out a big shout for 'no' as Root looks interested in a run.
Length and outside off, it's stroked through point for one.
Lovely shot from Root, for another two. Short in length and around off, Root turns inside the crease and pulls it in front of square on the leg side.
In the zone outside off, an easy leave for Ben Foakes.
Solid in defense. Around off, on a length, Ben offers a dead bat.
Fraction short and on off, Foakes punches from the back foot but finds the cover-point fielder.
Drifting down the leg side, Foakes gets across but fails to flick. It goes off his pads to fine leg and they take another two, this time as leg byes. 50 needed more.

That's a firm drive down the ground! Fuller and around off, Foakes forces it towards mid on where Southee dives across to his left and takes the pace off the ball. It rolls behind and the batters take two. England are dealing in couples this morning.
A gentle delivery, on a length around off and angling in, Ben gets across and helps it to short mid-wicket.
Change. Kyle Jamieson (20-4-59-4) comes into the attack now. He replaces Tim Southee.
Short in length and outside off, Root goes on the back foot and steers it past point and gets another brace. 54 needed more.
On a length and outside off, Root stays back and taps it down to gully.
Fine shot! The length is a shade too full, outside off, Root leans forward and drives it behind square on the off side. He gets a couple of runs.
Darts in a length ball on off, Root defends it from the back foot to the off side.
This time the line is a little too far outside off, Root offers no shot.
Boult straightaway begins from 'round the wicket angle. He serves it full and outside off, Root strides forward and pushes it defensively to covers.
Trent Boult to bowl from the other end. 20-3-61-1 are his figures so far.
Keeps probing with a length delivery, close to off, Foakes is again watchful in defense as he blocks it from the crease. 58 needed more.
Southee goes wide of the crease and angles in a length ball around off, Ben Foakes hangs on the back foot and defends it back.
Back of a length, on off, defended from the back foot to the off side.
Southee is too straight with his line, Foakes clips it off his pads behind square leg and collects a couple of runs.
Around off, on a good length, Foakes is on the back foot as he defends it on the leg side.
Southee begins with a length ball around off, Root shuffles across and nudges it down to fine leg. Takes a single, looks for the second run but it's not on. 60 more.

The morning session is set to begin on time, although it remains heavily overcast. The New Zealand players stride out to the middle. Followed by Joe Root and Ben Foakes who walk out to continue with their blade. It will be Tim Southee to start with the ball. Here we go...

Promising signs! The forecast isn't too great and the overhead conditions are gloomy but currently, it's not raining and the hover cover is not covering the pitch. Let's hope it stays this way and we get going on time. You already are aware of the equation needed, it looks quite straightforward but just for your reference, New Zealand lost 6 wickets yesterday for just 34 runs. If the Kiwi bowlers manage to strike the right chords and the overcast conditions come to their assistance, this little phase left in this Test match could become enthralling.

New Zealand, on the flip side, have a casualty in the form of Colin de Grandhomme after he limped off the field on Day 3. It is suspected that he has suffered a tear in his heel and we would get a better picture once the scheduled MRI scan is done. Coming to the game, the Kiwis would still believe that they can pull a rabbit out of the hat if they are able to get rid of Root early. Is there another twist left in this tale? Stick around to find out who will take the lead in this series.

Hello and a warm welcome to Day 4 of the first Test match between England and New Zealand. This match has surely moved briskly and it looks like England have their noses in front thanks to their former skipper, Joe Root. England are in contention of winning the game even after Kyle Jamieson's outstanding effort. The home side would hope that their lower-middle order along with Root is able to kick start their summer with a victory. Well, all this can happen only if the rain gods show some mercy.
... Day 4, Session 1...

The Kiwis just looked tired towards the end! Their bowlers did not bowl with the same energy, there were a few misfields too. They just had no answers to the batting of Root, Stokes of Foakes. However, they'll come all fresh on Day 4's morning, they would know a wicket and they'll be into the bowlers. The question is, who will get it for them? Day 4 promises to be a cracking on. Do join us for all the acion. Till then, take care and goodbye!

In reply, they were in big, big trouble at 69 for 4. It could have been worse had Colin not overstepped. Since then though, it has been all England. The skipper and the former skipper played brilliantly. The two added 90 before Stokes fell. Root though continued and along with Foakes has added another 50-run stand. The two have turned the game into England's favor.

End of a hard, fought day of Test cricket and we believe, England have their noses in front. A round of applause for England's former captain as he makes his way back into the dug out. We asked if England have it in them to show some character and fight to get back in the game and they surely do. First, they made quick work of the remaining wickets in the first session and kept the visitors in tact.
A single to end day's play! Short and on middle, this is pulled through square leg for one. THAT WILL BE STUMPS ON DAY 3!
Another short ball, another pull shot, through square leg for one.
That is a good short ball, on the body, Foakes evades it.
Short ball, this is pulled, off the back foot through square leg for one.
Two more! On middle, this is worked through mid-wicket. Two taken. Only 64 needed.
Well fielded! Length and on off, Root pushes it towards cover. The fielder dives to his left and stops it well.
Shorter and on off, Ben stands tall and pushes it to mid off.
On middle, this is dropped towards point for one.
Good length and around off, Root opens the face and guides it to point.
Well played again! On the pads, this is clipped through square leg for two. Fifty-run stand up between the two. A very important one but still, a lot of work left.
On middle, this is pushed to mid on.
Two more! Angled into the pads, Root clips it through square leg for two.
Bangs it short and on middle, Foakes ducks under it.
On off, Foakes plays it to covers.
Two more! Leg byes signaled! On the pads, Foakes looks to flick, it goes off the pads, down towards fine leg. Two taken.
On off, defended well.
From very wide of the crease. On a length and on off, kept out.
On off, this is kept out well.

EDGED BUT SHORT! A run as there is a misfield! On a length and around off, Foakes looks to block, it goes off the outside edge, lands short of the slip fielder. He lets it through and a single is taken.
Attacks the stumps again, Foakes keeps it out.
Goes wide of the crease and angles it into the off pole. Defended well.
On middle, Foakes plays it to mid on.
Outside off, left alone.
This is banged in short, on middle, Root pulls it through square leg for one.
Two leg byes! On the pads, Foakes looks to flick, misses, it hits the pad and goes behind. Two taken.
Shorter and around off, Foakes evades it.
On middle, this is clipped to mid-wicket.
On off, defended.
On middle, Foakes plays it to mid on.
Close! Outside off, once again comes back in but not enough to make the batter play.
Fuller and on off, Root comes down the track and looks to flick but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
FOUR! Almost drags it on! 200 up for England. Just the 77 needed! Shorter and outside off, Root looks to cut, it goes off the underedge, past the off pole and down to the fine leg fence.
On off, Root pushes it back to the bowler.
Shorter and down the leg side. Root evades it.
Fuller and on off, this is pushed back to the bowler.
Good length and on off, defended.
Shorter and on off, this is pushed to covers.
Outside off, comes back in with the angle. Not enough to make the batter play.
Too high! Length, on off, this one jags back in. Foakes misses the flick and is hit high on the pad. An appeal but turned down.
Misfield and more runs! Fuller and on off, this is hit towards mid off. Kane Williamson lets it through, he runs back and keeps it down to three.
Around off, this is guided to point.
On off, defended.
Kyle Jamieson is on now!
Outside off, left alone.
Agression from Southee! Fuller and on middle, this is hit back towards the bowler who has a shy at the keeper's end in anger but misses.
Down the leg side, Foakes looks to flick but misses.
On the pads, Root clips it through square leg for one.
FOUR MORE! Everything now going England's way! Just 85 needed! Shorter and outside off, Southee throws his bat at it, it goes off the outside edge, over gully and into the boundary.
FOUR! Angled into the pads, Root clips it throughs quare leg. It races away to the fence for a boundary.
Short and very wide outside off, Foakes looks to cut but ends up toe-ending it towards gully. That seemed like a tired ball.
On middle, Foakes plays it to mid on.
Fuller and on off, Foakes pushes it to covers.
Leading edge but just wide! Shorter and on off, Fokaes looks to work it on the leg side, he closes the face of the bat early. This flies off the leading edge wide of the fielder at point for two.
Angled into the pads, this is worked through square leg for one.
Around off, Root guides it to point.
On middle, defended.

Good fielding again but a single and Root brings his fifty up! Another superb knock from him and he probably holds the key for his side to win this game. On middle, this is worked towards square leg and a run is taken.
BEATEN! Good length and on off, this lands and moves away. Root is beaten as he tries to defend.
Back of a length and on off, kept out.
On the middle pole, this is worked wide of mid on for one.
On a length and on leg, Joe Root flicks it towards square leg and gets a single.
Well stopped! On the pads, this is clipped through square leg. Ajaz dives to his right and saves three.
Outside off, this is guided through point for one.
Shorter and on middle, Foakes ducks under it.
Well left! Outside off, not played at.
On the pads, this is clipped to mid-wicket.
On middle, this is pushed to mid on for one.
Good length and on off, kept out.
Outside off, left alone.
Now takes one as this is worked through mid-wicket.
FOUR! Up and over! Thickish edge and it goes over the fielders! Shorter and outside off, Root slashes, it goes over gully for a boundary in the third man region.
On off, defended.
Tw more! On middle, this is worked through mid-wicket for two.
On off, this is pushed towards mid off for one.
BYE! A big inswinger but down the leg side. Blundell does well to dive to his left and get a hand to it. A bye taken.
On middle, this is worked to mid-wicket.
Back of a length and on off, defended.
Angles this one away, lands it on off. Blocked out.
Shorter and on middle, this is pulled through square leg for one.
Gets this one to tail back in, lands it on middle, defended.
On off, this is pushed to covers.
On off, defended.
Angled into the middle pole, this is worked through mid-wicket for one.
Outside off and on a length, left alone again.
Good length and on off, defended.
Shot! Fuller and on off, Foakes leans into it and strokes it past mid off for two.
Outside off, Root now pushes it through covers for one.
Foakes is off the mark! Shorter and on off, Foakes guides it towards point and takes one.
BEATEN! Bowls the one that goes away. Length and on off, this lands and moves away. Foakes is beaten as he tries to defend.
Fuller and on off, Root pushes it towards cover for one.
Good length and on off, defended.

OUT! GLOVED AND TAKEN! That is a massive, massive breakthrough and who else provides the breakthrough? It is Kyle Jamieson! Stokes will be disappointed. THe game was actually coming into his side's control but he falls. This is short and it is angled into the body. There was not enough room to play the upper cut but Stokes still goes for it. It goes off the glove and Tom Blundell takes it by moving to his right. Stokes walks back gutted. Will this open the floodgates now? New Zealand are only a wicket away from entering the bowlers.
Commentary.Howout: c Tom Blundell b Kyle Jamieson

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and on middle, Joe Root clips it towards square leg for one.
Length ball outside off, Ben Stokes cuts it through point for one.
Fuller and on middle, this is defended out.
On middle, blocked out.
On middle, Ben Stokes flicks it towards square leg for a boundary. 27th test fifty for Ben Stokes and his first test fifty as a captain.
Fuller and on middle, this is flicked towards mid on for one. Brilliant over for England.
FOUR BYES! On middle, Ben Stokes again tries for a slog sweep but gets his pads. The ball races past long stop for a boundary.
SIX! This was similar to the last maximum. On middle, Ben Stokes again slog sweeps it over deep square leg for a maximum.
On middle, blocked out.
SIX! Full and on middle, Ben Stokes slog sweeps it over deep square leg for a biggie.
Tossed up on middle, Ben Stokes eases it towards mid on.

A bit of spin now as Ajaz Patel is brought into the attack. Also, the physio is out and having a word with Joe Root. Root seems to be hurt on his finger on the right hand in the last over. Root gets a painkiller and is good to continue.
On middle angling it in, Joe Root blocks it back towards the bowler.
Length ball outside off, Joe Root punches it straight towards the fielder at point.
Back of a length and on leg, this is blocked out towards the vacant short leg region.
On a length and outside off, Joe Root guides it straight towards the fielder at point.
Kyle Jamieson sees Stokes advancing and goes fuller and on leg, Ben Stokes guides it towards backward point and gets a single.
Back of a length and on off, Ben Stokes leaves it alone.
Touch fuller and on leg, Ben Stokes flicks it towards backward square leg for one.
Goes full and outside off, Ben Stokes blocks it away.
Full and outside leg, Joe Root looks to flick it but misses. The keeper just manages to get his glove on it. The batters cross and a bye is signaled.
On middle, Joe Root blocks it away.
Length ball and outside off, Joe Root has a poke at it but misses. The ball just zipped past the outside edge and straight into the gloves of the keeper. Joe Root gets a lucky escape.
Fuller and outside off, Joe Root leaves it alone.
On middle, Ben Stokes blocks it out solidly.

FIVE WIDES! Fuller and wide outside leg, Ben Stokes looks to give a fine tickle but misses. The keeper misses the ball as it just keeps on swinging downhill. The ball races past the long stop for a boundary.
Outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, Ben Stokes looks to drive it but misses. The ball just aired past his bat and straight into the gloves of the keeper.
FOUR! On a length and outside off, Ben Stokes dances down the track and smashes it through covers for a boundary.
On middle, defended out.
On a length and on middle, Ben Stokes defends it towards short mid-wicket.
A slight halt in play as the batters have a bit of a breather and the 12th man runs out with drinks.
On a good length and outside off, Joe Root leaves it alone.
On middle, this is flicked towards square leg for one.
Outside off, Ben Stokes leaves it alone.
On a length and angled into the leg stump, Ben Stokes gets hurried on as the ball skids through and hits him high on the pads.
Full and on the stumps, Ben Stokes eases it towards the mid on region.
Length ball on middle and leg, Ben Stokes blocks it towards mid on.
Goes full and outside off, Joe Root leaves it alone.
On middle, Joe Root drives it through wide mid on for a brace.
FOUR! On middle and slightly shorter, Joe Root pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary. 50 partnership comes up for Joe Root and Ben Stokes.
On a good length and on middle, this is pushed back towards the bowler.
Another one outside off, not played at.
Slower and outside off, Joe Root leaves it alone towards the keeper.
Another one on middle, blocked towards mid on.
Touch fuller and on middle, Ben Stokes defends it towards the mid off region.
Length ball outside off, Ben Stokes doesn't bother it.
Full and straight at the stumps, Joe Root flicks it towards mid-wicket for one.
On middle, defended out.

Back of a length and on middle, Joe Root pulls it towards mid-wicket. Good fielding from the fielder. Ben Stokes wanted a single but goes back and unknowingly blocks a direct hit on the way. Trent Boult and Ben Stokes have a good laugh over it. He was safe anyways.

It was the Jamieson show as he got the better of Bairstow and Crawley. Boult also chipped in with a wicket. However, New Zealand will know it is important to break this stand. The two are well set and have done well so far but if England are to have any chance, they need to play for a long time. Can they do so? We will find out in the next session.

The pitch is offering something for the bowlers but it is still a good one to bat on. New Zealand need to continue to hit the right areas and they will be eager for a couple of wickets after the break. England on the other hand, would hope these two can build a decent stand and lay the platform for their side. A very interesting session awaits. Do join us in sometime.

Excellent session of Test cricket! Have to say it has been England's morning. After pickings wickets in a flurry this morning, the hosts kept England well in-tact. They had just below an hour to play out before Lunch. Lees and Crawley began brilliantly. They played their shots and Lees was scoring freely. Kyle Jamieson it was though again who got the opening breakthrough for his side. Since then, the runs have dried out and New Zealand have started to cause problems too.
